title: Admin proxy for guarded runbook execution and dry-run safety
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: On-call engineers and support SREs frequently run ad-hoc admin scripts and runbook steps directly on clusters or via the admin CLI. This causes three recurring issues: noisy retries and throttling against downstream control planes, lack of consistent RBAC/enforcement, and gaps in auditability for quick post-incident reviews.

Goal: Build a lightweight Admin Proxy service that fronts runbook execution and admin utilities, providing: 1) guarded execution modes (dry-run / confirm / safe-exec), 2) per-principal rate limiting and cooldowns to prevent thundering herds, 3) structured outputs and standardized exit metadata for Console ingestion, 4) shallow task semantics to allow runbooks-as-tasks (idempotent steps with replayable inputs), and 5) audit logs and tracing hooks integrated into Console and our KMS-backed log store.

Scope for this ticket: MVP proxy runtime and CLI shim integration (no on-prem agent in scope). Deliver a proxy that supports a defined subset of admin commands (cluster-cordon, restart-service, scale-deployment, clear-cache) and can be extended with new command handlers via a small handler interface. The service must provide dry-run and confirmation tokens, and expose metrics for rate-limit hits and dry-run traffic.

Out of scope: full on-prem daemon, complex orchestration UIs, advanced orchestration (A/B canary flows). Those will follow in future tickets once the handler abstraction and audit pipeline are validated.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts authenticated requests from ops-cli and returns a structured JSON response with status, actions, and a run_id
Dry-run mode returns no side effects and lists the concrete API calls that would run; smoke-run returns a safe subset of effects
Per-principal rate limits configurable via Console and enforced with token buckets; default limits documented
Audit events (run_id, actor, inputs, result, confirmation_token) are persisted to KMS-backed audit store and visible in Console traces
Minimal handler contract implemented and three handlers (cordon, restart-service, scale-deployment) wired, with tests
E2E tests and a load test demonstrating safe-mode noop latency p95 < 300ms under 50 concurrent dry-run requests
Migration guide and new runbook templates published in Confluence and linked from Console runbook panel
design_notes:
Architecture sketch: an HTTP/GRPC proxy with a lightweight handler registry. Each handler implements validate(inputs), simulate(inputs) and execute(inputs). The proxy authenticates via existing ops service tokens (short-lived), checks RBAC using the RBAC service, applies rate limits (redis token bucket) and then either simulates or enqueues execution. For sync commands we support immediate execution with confirmation tokens. For longer-running operations we return a run_id and push progress events to the events stream for Console consumption.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Full task queue vs sync proxy — choose hybrid: sync for quick ops, background queue for heavier work to avoid blocking clients. 2) Centralized handler registry vs decentralized agents — start centralized to keep audit and rate-limits in one place for MVP. 3) Persisting audit logs in S3 vs KMS-protected DB — chosen KMS-protected append-only store for easy querying in Console while meeting compliance.

Operational concerns: rate-limit misconfiguration could block oncall; default limits must be conservative and changeable via Console. We will add a feature flag to bypass rate-limits for emergency SRE role (audited).
implementation_plan: 1) API design and proto: define /run, /simulate, /status endpoints and run metadata. 2) Implement core proxy with handler registry and RBAC checks. 3) Wire 3 handlers and add unit/integration tests. 4) Implement redis-backed rate limiter and metrics. 5) Hook audit events to KMS store and Console traces. 6) Publish CLI shim changes and docs. 7) Run staged rollout (internal only -> canary -> org-wide).
testing_plan: Unit tests for handler contract. Integration tests that exercise dry-run vs execute paths against a test cluster. Load tests (k6) to validate rate limiting and p95 latency goals. Chaos tests to ensure confirmation tokens prevent accidental double-execution. Post-deploy: monitor rate-limit metrics and error rates in Sentry and Console dashboards.
rollout_and_migration: Initial rollout: internal ops team only with feature flag. Use canary pool of 5 engineers to validate behavior and collect feedback. After 1 week and zero critical issues, expand to all SREs. Migration steps for existing runbooks: add a small adapter layer to call the proxy simulate() path and verify outputs before switching execution to execute().
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: proxy becomes single point of failure. Mitigation: run proxy in HA across regions, introduce fallback path that allows local CLI to execute with additional audit markers. Risk: rate limits block incident remediation. Mitigation: emergency-bypass role with strict audit and alerting. Risk: handler bugs cause unintended side effects. Mitigation: require unit tests for each handler, staged rollout, pre-exec confirmation token.
open_decisions: 1) Persistence format for audit events (JSONL vs protobuf) — leaning JSONL for human-readability. 2) Whether to allow nested multi-step runbooks in MVP — defer. 3) Emergency bypass UX in Console: button vs CLI token — prefer CLI token for traceability.
notes: Related docs: Confluence: /ops/admin-proxy-spec (draft), Design doc PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-proxy/pull/182. Early spike showed dry-run simulation for scale-deployment can be implemented by validating desired replica count and checking cluster autoscaler policies. Estimated infra cost impact < 5% of current admin traffic.
